extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent applicants/attorneys (patent practitioners)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive guidance from MPEP Chapter 700 on examination of patent applications, including filing-date/requisite rules, searching, handling informal disclosures, and requirements for information under 37 CFR 1.105. Intended to direct examiners and inform applicants about examination practice and required responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory authority for examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination authority derives from 35 U.S.C. 131 (Director shall cause an examination) and the main conditions precedent for grant are set forth in 35 U.S.C. 101, 102, 103, and 112.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If on examination the applicant is entitled to a patent under the law, the Director shall issue a patent. See related MPEP sections for further statutory interpretation (e.g., §§ 2104–2109, 2157).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions relevant to examination (35 U.S.C. 100)
rubrics_metrics.description: Key statutory definitions (e.g., 'invention', 'process', 'United States', 'patentee', 'third-party requester', 'inventor', 'joint inventor', 'joint research agreement', 'effective filing date', 'claimed invention') determine application treatment and rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective filing date rules (including priority/benefit dates) and claimed invention definitions are used to determine entitlement and applicable law (AIA vs pre-AIA). See MPEP for applicability nuances (PLTIA impact).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing-date and requisites of the application (post-PLTIA)
rubrics_metrics.description: For nonprovisional applications filed on/after Dec 18, 2013 (PLTIA/PLT implementation), the filing date (except design) is the date a specification, with or without claims, is received in the Office; drawings are not always required except where necessary for understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design applications differ. Inclusion of claims/drawings remains prudent to ensure disclosure satisfies 35 U.S.C. 112(a) and 113; OPAP reviews completeness (fees, oath/declaration, all pages) and issues notices for incomplete filings. Applications without at least one claim may receive an OPAP notice to submit a claim to avoid abandonment; examiners will not docket an application until it includes specification and at least one claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPAP completeness check and notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Office of Patent Application Processing (OPAP) determines entitlement to filing date and whether the application papers are complete (fees, oath/declaration, pages).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not entitled to a filing date, OPAP sends 'Notice of Incomplete Application'; if entitled but incomplete, sends 'Notice of Omitted Item(s)'. Examiner should determine whether the application is complete when taken up for examination and act accordingly (see §§ 601.01(d),(g)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiners ensure application is complete before examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner should verify that the application is complete when taken up for examination and determine actions if specification pages or drawings are missing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §§ 601.01(d) and 601.01(g) for guidance on actions when pages/drawings are missing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimal formal requirements are not best-practice prescriptions
rubrics_metrics.description: The PLT/PLTIA minimal filing requirements should not be viewed as prescribing best practice for preparing and filing patent applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are advised to include claims and drawings where relevant; preparing claims at filing helps ensure compliance with 35 U.S.C. 112(a) and submitting necessary drawings helps satisfy 35 U.S.C. 113.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of obviously informal cases
rubrics_metrics.description: When disclosure is informal or insufficient to permit a complete merits action, examiner may follow specified procedure (reasonable search, include form listing informalities, require revision to idiomatic English, reject informal claims under 35 U.S.C. 112).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure elements: (A) make reasonable search to extent possible (if incomprehensible, inform applicant that no search was made); (B) include form listing informalities and formal requirements in first Office action (see form paragraph references); (C) require spec revision to idiomatic English and U.S. practice; (D) reject claims failing to define invention per 35 U.S.C. 112—blanket rejection usually sufficient. Examiner should point out informality points; applicant bears burden to revise; multiple obviously informal claims treated as a single claim for fee/exam purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary amendments in informal cases (no new matter)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are urged to submit a preliminary amendment promptly (preferably within 3 months after filing) to correct obvious informalities; amendments must exclude 'new matter'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary amendments filed after filing date do not enjoy original disclosure status; see MPEP § 608.04(b). Amend informalities so disclosure and initial claims are understandable and properly dependent/definite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of form paragraph 7.01 (unconventional terminology)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 7.01 is used when terminology is so different from art-accepted terminology that a proper prior-art search cannot be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form requires applicant to clarify or correlate terminology with art-accepted terms and warns about not introducing new matter. A shortened statutory period for reply (TWO MONTHS) is set. Examiner notes indicate bracketed text to specify problematic terminology and pages, and cross-references to drawing procedures (MPEP §§ 608.02(a),(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of form paragraph 7.02 (disclosure incomprehensible)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 7.02 is used where disclosure is so incomprehensible that a reasonable search cannot be made; it lists specific items not understood and requires amendment to clarify.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant warned not to introduce new matter; shortened statutory period for reply (TWO MONTHS) set. Examiner should indicate pages/features not understood. See cross-references for idiomatic English form paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of forms 7.31.01–7.31.04 for claim rejections based on deficiencies
rubrics_metrics.description: When rejecting claims due to disclosure deficiencies as described in form paragraphs (e.g., 7.01/7.02), use the appropriate 7.31.xx form paragraphs for claim rejections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms provide standardized wording and examiner notes for using rejections tied to disclosure deficiencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: When terminology not consonant with the art
rubrics_metrics.description: If terms/phrases/modes of characterization are not consonant with the relevant art (so examiner cannot perform 37 CFR 1.104 examination), the examiner should make a reasonable search to extent possible and request applicant correlate terminology with art-accepted terminology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If proper search cannot be made, use form paragraph 7.01. Examiner may limit action to citing most pertinent prior art and requesting terminology correlation before further action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search duties before examination (MPEP § 704.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: After reading the specification and claims, the examiner searches prior art; the invention should be thoroughly understood before the search. Informal or imperfectly understood cases also receive searches to avoid piecemeal prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Chapter 900 (esp. §§ 904–904.03) for searching details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of a previous examiner's search
rubrics_metrics.description: When acting on an application with prior examiner actions, the new examiner should review the previous search to ensure thoroughness and generally should not take an entirely new approach or reorient the point of view merely to try to find something new.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 904.02 and § 719.05 for principles; maintain continuity unless clear reason to change approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to require information (37 CFR 1.105)
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner or other Office employee may require submission of information from individuals identified under 37 CFR 1.56(c), any assignee, or obligated assignee, that is reasonably necessary to properly examine or treat a matter in pending/abandoned applications, patents, or reexaminations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authority arises from 35 U.S.C. 131 and 132 and Director/TC policies. The scope extends to assignees and obligated assignees because they may hold relevant knowledge. Star Fruits case supports Office ability to compel disclosure under 1.105.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of information that may be required under 37 CFR 1.105(a)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Enumerated examples include: (i) existence of particularly relevant commercial databases known to inventors; (ii) whether a prior-art search was made and what was searched; (iii) copies of non-patent literature/published applications/patents by any inventor that relate to the claimed invention; (iv) literature used to draft the application; (v) literature used in the invention process (e.g., to design around); (vi) identification of what is being improved where claimed invention is an improvement; (vii) identification of any use of the claimed invention known to inventors at filing; (viii) technical information known to applicant concerning related art, disclosure, claimed subject matter, or accuracy of examiner interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These examples are illustrative, not exhaustive. Requirements should narrow focus and be reasonably based on examination needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible formats for requirements for factual information
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements may be presented as a requirement for factual information, interrogatories (specific questions), or stipulations as to facts for applicant to agree/disagree with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any reply stating the information is unknown or not readily available may be accepted as a complete reply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion and timing of requirements for information
rubrics_metrics.description: A requirement under 37 CFR 1.105(a)(1) may be included in an Office action or sent separately; replies or failures to reply are governed by 37 CFR §§ 1.135 and 1.136.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should clearly focus the reason and scope of the requirement and ensure compliance with reply-time procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and standard for requiring information (reasonable necessity)
rubrics_metrics.description: A requirement may only be made when the examiner has a reasonable basis that the information is 'reasonably necessary' to examine or treat the matter; the requirement places a substantial burden on applicant and therefore should be narrowly defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terms 'factual' and 'facts' clarify that the Office seeks facts known to applicant or readily obtainable after reasonable inquiry, not opinions; applicant need not derive facts by experimentation. The purpose is to improve patent quality and decisions, not to jeopardize applicant's duty of candor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information reasonably necessary for finding prior art is not a substitute for examiner search
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for information to find prior art do not replace the examiner's obligation to perform a search; examiner must still perform a search per MPEP §§ 704.01 and 904–904.03.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The requirement is appropriate in specific situations (see criteria) to supplement examiner search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria where requirement for information is generally justified
rubrics_metrics.description: A requirement for information is generally reasonably necessary when: (A) the claimed subject matter cannot be adequately searched by class or keyword among patents and typical NPL sources, or (B) the application file or the lack of relevant prior art found in the examiner's search suggests the applicant likely has access to information relevant to patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First instance typically occurs for inventions in new tech areas lacking classification; second when related applications/publications by applicant indicate they may know additional relevant info.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of additional information that may be reasonably required (704.11(a) list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-exhaustive examples include: (A) name/citation of any particularly relevant indexed journal or treatise; (B) trade name of goods/services embodying claimed subject matter; (C) citation/dates/copies of advertising/promotional literature for goods/services; (E) trade names and providers of competing goods/services; (F) any written descriptions/analyses by inventors/assignees about competing goods/services; (G) identification of pending or abandoned applications by inventors/assignee that disclose similar subject matter not identified in current application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These examples guide examiners on the type of factual documentary/material information that an applicant may reasonably be expected to provide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replies to requirements for information — reasonable inquiry obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant is expected to make a reasonable inquiry under applicable rules (e.g., 37 CFR 11.18(b)(2)) to determine factual information; but applicant need not experimentally derive facts in response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If information is unknown or not readily available, a reply stating so may be accepted as complete. Responses must be factual rather than opinion-based.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement scope should be narrowly focused and have reasonable basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Because requirements impose substantial burden, examiners must clearly focus the reason for the requirement and the scope of the expected response and only make requirements when a reasonable basis exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overbroad or speculative requests are inappropriate; documentation/examples in the office action should justify the specific information requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of 1.105 scope to assignees and obligated assignees
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.105 authority extends to assignees and anyone obligated to assign the application because information required may be known to assignee members even if not known by inventors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner may require information from those parties where reasonable necessity is demonstrated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time period for reply when using certain form paragraphs
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraphs used for unconventional terminology or incomprehensible disclosure set a shortened statutory period for reply (TWO MONTHS from mailing date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner notes in forms indicate how to fill bracketed items and cross-refer to drawing sufficiency procedures where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treating multiple obviously informal claims as single claim for fees/exam
rubrics_metrics.description: If a number of obviously informal claims are filed, such claims should be treated as being a single claim for fee and examination purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reduces applicant burden when claims are manifestly informal and avoids unfair fees for obviously defective claim sets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correlation request when lack of art-accepted terminology prevents search
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner finds that terminology prevents a proper search, the Office action should require applicant to correlate terminology with art-accepted terminology prior to further action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.01 where applicable and explain page references and problematic terms; warn about not submitting new matter.
